review_scope: Existing Figma design (~6 months old, predates this feature's PRD/research/strategy) — Figma file 'Dune Security (Master file)', page 'DUNE 628 - Custom Creation of phishing Assets': the Simulated Attacks Library entry point and the full Create New Asset flow across all three creation tabs (Generate with AI, Create Manually, Upload EML File), inspected live via Figma Desktop Bridge across 9 screen frames plus library list states and a flattened flow-diagram image.
rebuild_note: 2026-07-09 — All 10 findings addressed in a rebuilt storyboard on the same Figma page, in a new section named 'AI Phishing Template Generator — Rebuilt Storyboard (2026-07-09)', positioned below the original (untouched) content for direct comparison. 14 screens total: the 6 original screens fixed in place (Generate with AI setup + edit, Upload EML setup + edit, Create Manually, Library happy path) plus 8 new screens/states (Generating progress, Regenerate confirm modal, Mobile preview variant, Library empty state, Library view-only/RBAC state, Template Detail with deploy enabled, Template Detail with deploy disabled/RBAC, Delete confirm modal). See findings[].outcome for per-finding resolution and revised_verdict for the rebuild's standing.
quality_bar_assessment: Structural craft is good (tab model, calm intro banner, single-page progressive disclosure), but the design falls short of Stripe-level craft on trust communication and state completeness: no visible confirmation that redaction or safe-link rewriting occurred, no generation-progress feedback for a ~10s AI call, and a WYSIWYG editor that silently degrades to raw HTML for one of three creation modes.
strengths: Single-page progressive-disclosure creation model (prompt/upload to generate to same-screen edit) is more efficient than a multi-screen wizard and worth preserving

Existing Simulated Attacks Library (table, search, Sender/Difficulty/Motive/Method/Vector filters, Email/SMS/Voice/Hybrid/Custom Assets tabs) is a mature surface this feature should extend rather than duplicate
Existing 'Motive' taxonomy (Authority, etc.) already echoes AEP Builder's Adversary Method concept, a cross-feature consistency opportunity already half-built
In-body 'Add Phishing Link' and 'Add QR code' authoring tools are a thoughtful, already-solved capability not addressed in the current PRD
Intro banner framing AI vs. manual creation sets expectations clearly and calmly across all three tabs

findings.location: Generate with AI / Create Manually / Upload EML File tabs — Difficulty dropdown
findings.issue: Difficulty is set after generation and never appears wired into the generation call itself; it remains unset in every post-generation frame observed.
findings.why_it_matters: The PRD requires difficulty to shape generated content via agentic reasoning, not just classify it afterward — a template labeled 'Hard' may never have been generated with hard-difficulty characteristics.
findings.recommended_fix: Move Difficulty above the generate action so it's a generation input, or explicitly document that it's a post-hoc library tag if that's intentional.
principles: Match between system and the real world
findings.teaching_note: A control positioned like an input but behaving like a label is a quiet trust gap in an AI feature — verify causality, not just placement.
findings.resolution: Difficulty moved above the Generate/Upload action on all three creation setup screens, defaulted to Medium, with helper text framing it as a generation input; the Edit screen's Difficulty is now paired with an explicit Regenerate action rather than auto-applying.

findings.location: All three Create New Asset tabs — Preview panel
findings.issue: No desktop/mobile preview toggle exists anywhere in the reviewed frames; Preview always renders a single fixed-width view.
findings.why_it_matters: This is a named PRD acceptance criterion, and most target employees open simulations on mobile — analysts can't verify mobile rendering before a template goes live.
findings.recommended_fix: Add a desktop/mobile toggle to the Preview panel header.
findings.teaching_note: A preview that only shows one viewport is half a preview for anything destined for an inbox.
findings.resolution: Added a Desktop/Mobile segmented toggle to the Preview panel header on both edit screens; built a dedicated Mobile Preview screen showing the narrower rendering with wrapped body text.

findings.location: Upload EML File tab, Body editor (frame 13947:20653)
findings.issue: After .eml upload, the Body editor shows raw HTML source markup instead of the rendered email that the other two creation modes show in the same component.
findings.why_it_matters: Breaks the WYSIWYG promise specifically for the mode the PRD frames as fast and low-skill; editing raw HTML risks breaking the email's rendering entirely.
findings.recommended_fix: Parse and render uploaded .eml HTML into the same WYSIWYG canvas used by the other modes, with an explicit fallback state if rendering fails.
principles: Match between system and the real world
findings.teaching_note: When one of three parallel paths through a shared component behaves differently with no visible reason, assume it's an unhandled edge case until proven otherwise.
findings.resolution: The rebuilt Upload EML edit screen shows fully rendered body content (verified via screenshot — a rendered Zendesk-branded email, not raw markup); the redundant duplicate frame that had shown raw HTML was removed from the rebuilt storyboard entirely.

findings.location: All Create New Asset tabs — Preview panel and Body editor, post-generation/upload
findings.issue: No visible confirmation that sensitive data was redacted or links rewritten to safe URLs; placeholder tokens use two inconsistent, unstyled syntaxes ({{firstname}} vs __FIRST_NAME__ __LAST_NAME__).
findings.why_it_matters: Redaction and safe-link rewriting are the feature's core safety claims; an analyst has no way to visually verify either happened.
findings.recommended_fix: Unify placeholder token syntax and styling across all creation modes; add an explicit post-generation confirmation (e.g., 'Links converted to safe simulation URLs').
findings.teaching_note: A safety claim with no visible evidence is functionally no safety claim, from a trust standpoint.
findings.resolution: Added a green confirmation line under the Preview header on both edit screens: '✓ Sensitive data redacted · Links converted to safe simulation URLs'. Placeholder token syntax unification across modes was not completed (tracked as a residual item, not blocking).

findings.location: Transition from clicking Generate Asset to the Preview/Edit reveal
findings.issue: No loading, progress, or labeled-stage state exists anywhere between submitting input and seeing the generated result.
findings.why_it_matters: A ~10s wait with no progress feedback reads as broken, especially against Dune's own established AEP Builder labeled-progress pattern for a similar wait.
findings.recommended_fix: Reuse AEP Builder's labeled advancing-stage progress pattern, named after what generation actually does.
findings.teaching_note: Any async action in the 3-15 second range needs a designed waiting state; silence reads as failure.
findings.resolution: Added a new Generating screen with 5 labeled advancing stages (Analyzing input, Drafting template, Redacting sensitive data, Rewriting links to safe URLs, Ready), matching the AEP Builder precedent named in the original review.

findings.location: Create New Asset — all three tabs
findings.issue: No field labeled Template Name/Asset Title exists on any creation tab, though the Library has a Title column; unclear whether Title is auto-derived from the email Subject.
findings.why_it_matters: Conflates the internal library name with the user-facing bait subject line, and leaves the PRD's open duplicate-name question with no field to validate against.
findings.recommended_fix: Add an explicit Template Name field, separate from Subject, on all three tabs.
findings.teaching_note: Any object with a library/list view needs an explicit name field distinct from its user-facing content.
findings.resolution: Added an explicit Template Name field, separate from Subject, at the top of all three creation tabs and the two edit screens, with helper text clarifying its purpose (finding the template in the library later).

findings.issue: Body field is pre-filled with the same fixture content as the AI-generated example rather than starting blank or with a minimal scaffold.
findings.why_it_matters: Likely a mock artifact, but as designed undermines the tab's 'full control' value proposition since it looks identical to the AI output.
findings.recommended_fix: Confirm this is fixture reuse; design an explicit blank/scaffold starting state for manual creation if intended.
principles: Match between system and the real world
findings.teaching_note: Reused mock content is easy to mistake for a real default; flag it explicitly in the file.
findings.resolution: Create Manually's body canvas now starts genuinely blank with placeholder guidance text ('Start writing your email...'); Sender Name, Subject, and the Preview panel were all reset to blank/placeholder state to match.

findings.location: Generate with AI tab, Select motive field (frame 5040:166284)
findings.issue: Field labeled 'Select motive' displays 'Sender' as its value instead of a motive-type value like 'Authority'.
findings.why_it_matters: Reads as a copy-paste wiring bug that would confuse a reviewer or engineer during handoff.
findings.recommended_fix: Correct the displayed value to match the Motive taxonomy and QA this control before handoff.
findings.teaching_note: Small mismatches are cheap to fix now and expensive to discover during dev handoff.
findings.resolution: The Select motive field now displays 'Authority' (a real motive value matching the Library's own Motive taxonomy) instead of 'Sender'.

findings.issue: No view-only, restricted-action, or disabled/tooltip states found anywhere; Save Asset is always enabled and the post-save toast shows the asset already Active with no visible deploy gate.
findings.why_it_matters: The PRD requires RBAC gating of view/edit/deploy as potentially separable actions; this design shows a simpler, ungated Save-to-Active model.
findings.recommended_fix: Confirm with PM whether Active-on-save is intentional or whether a downstream deploy gate exists elsewhere; design explicit RBAC states either way.
findings.teaching_note: Absence of RBAC states in a mock isn't proof RBAC is unhandled — confirm before treating it as a gap to design versus a gap to document.
findings.resolution: Added a Library view-only state (no Create/Request action, explicit 'View-only access' label) and a new Template Detail screen with two RBAC variants: Use in Campaign enabled, and disabled at 40% opacity with a 'You don't have permission to deploy templates' tooltip-style note. The underlying product question — whether Active-on-save is intentional or a downstream deploy gate exists elsewhere — is still open and listed below.

findings.location: Upload EML File tab, Body editor helper text
findings.issue: Helper text reads literally 'This is a hint text to help user.' — unfinished placeholder copy.
findings.why_it_matters: Low severity alone, but signals this file needs a copy pass before reuse.
findings.teaching_note: Placeholder copy left for six months is a good prompt to do a full copy audit before treating any part of a file as handoff-ready.
findings.resolution: Replaced all instances of 'This is a hint text to help user.' across Sender email, Sender Name, Subject, and Difficulty fields on every screen with real, field-specific guidance copy.

open_questions: [Design] Does this Figma page reflect the current production experience, or is it a superseded/parked exploration?

[PM] Is Active status on save the intended final state, or is there a downstream deploy/campaign-attach gate not visible in this file? The rebuild adds RBAC-gated deploy states on a new Template Detail screen but does not resolve this underlying product question.

[Design] Should this feature's library be the existing multi-channel Simulated Attacks Library rather than the standalone Template Library proposed in design-strategy.md? The rebuild extends the existing library directly (empty + view-only states added to it), which implicitly answers this in favor of reuse — confirm with the team before treating it as final.
[Design] Placeholder token syntax ("{{firstname}}" vs "__FIRST_NAME__") was not unified across creation modes in the rebuild — worth a follow-up pass.

[Design] Regenerate and Delete buttons reuse the same primary green button style since no destructive/red variant exists in this file's component set — confirm whether a true destructive style should be added to the DS.
revision_priorities: Resolve the Active-on-save vs. downstream-deploy-gate product question with PM (open, not a design fix)
Confirm the Simulated Attacks Library reuse direction with the team (open, not a design fix)
Unify placeholder token syntax and add a true destructive button style to the DS (residual polish, non-blocking)
